title: Adversarial Gradient Driven Exploration for Deep Click-Through Rate Prediction

problem.claim: Large-scale online recommender systems must address feedback-loop effects while balancing exploration and exploitation.

gap.claim: Uncertainty-focused exploration overlooks how exploration changes collected training data and subsequent model learning.

contributions.claim: A Pseudo-Exploration module simulates model updating after an item is explored and feedback is received.
AGE uses the equivalence between the simulated updating process and an adversarial perturbation to the model input.
A dynamic gating unit pre-determines exploration utility to allocate limited exploration resources and avoid ineffective exploration.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive ablation studies on an academic dataset were used to examine AGE's effectiveness.
AGE was deployed on a world-leading display advertising platform, where the authors observed significant improvements on various top-line evaluation metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Exploration-exploitation algorithms address feedback-loop issues in online recommender systems.
Existing uncertainty-centered approaches underconsider the effects of exploration on training data and model learning.
The work simulates post-exploration model updates and relates them to adversarial input perturbations, yielding AGE.
A dynamic gate estimates exploration utility for more selective resource use.
The authors report academic ablations and deployment results with improvements in top-line metrics.

source_observation.claim: Exploration changes the training data collected and therefore can affect model learning.

interpretation.claim: Exploration policies should be evaluated partly for their downstream training effects, not only for estimated uncertainty.

application.claim: When designing online-learning exploration, model both immediate selection utility and the consequences for future data collection.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this principle generalizes beyond the reported recommender and advertising settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the AGE objective, optimization details, or model architecture.
The abstract does not provide dataset sizes, baselines, metric values, or statistical procedures.
The abstract does not describe the deployment period, traffic scale, or operational constraints.
